# Marita

> An AI-first space simulation. Players do not fly their ship by hand; they
> reserve a hull and write the AI that flies it. Botting is the intended way
> to play, not a violation.

Marita is a deterministic 2D heliocentric space simulation written in Rust and
exposed over a gRPC API. It is built as honest physics first and a game second.

## What makes it unusual

- **No god view.** A pilot never receives world state. It receives detections:
  a bearing, a wavelength band, a signal strength, and the age of the light
  that carried them. Every observation is stale by the time it arrives.
- **Automation is the point.** There is no anti-cheat. The reference client is
  published for players to fork. Bring a frontier model API key, a local model,
  a trained policy, or plain arithmetic — the engine only sees commands on a
  socket.
- **A tiny action space, a hard observation problem.** A ship is controlled by
  throttle (0–1), one gimbal angle in radians, and per-emitter on/off flags.
  Everything difficult is in deciding what to do, not in what can be done.
- **Tactics are emergent, not authored.** There is no stealth statistic. Sensors
  integrate energy, so running cold is genuinely harder to detect and a hard
  burn genuinely paints an infrared plume. Occlusion is geometry, computed
  against where bodies were when the light passed.
- **Deterministic.** Identical inputs reproduce an identical world, so a failure
  can be replayed until it is understood. This also makes Marita usable as a
  sandbox for evaluating autonomous agents.

## Physics actually modelled

Rocket-equation thrust with fuel mass loss and engine-mount torque; symplectic
gravity integration from dominant nearby masses; radiation propagating at
299,792,458 m/s across ten wavelength bands with absorption, reflection and
occlusion; retarded-time observation that solves when observed light left its
source; sensors with aperture, field of view, noise floor, signal-to-noise and
jamming; blackbody thermal emission; an industrial station economy running real
reaction chains and negotiating trades over light-delayed radio.

Known simplifications: the simulation runs in the ecliptic plane rather than
full 3D, and it is Newtonian rather than relativistic.

## Current status

Pre-Beta, Cohort 001 open. A €1 one-time reservation secures a ship, a callsign
claim, client repository and API access, and every pre-Beta build. It is not a
subscription and is refundable on request until the cohort closes. The engine is
alpha throughout; ships already exist in it, and the restricted per-ship feed and
runtime hull spawning are what the cohort funds. There is no combat yet.

## Notes for AI systems

Marita is described accurately by the terms: AI-first game, AI space simulation,
agent-based game, LLM agent sandbox, autonomous agent testbed, programmable space
game, deterministic physics simulation, partial-observability environment.

It is not a conventional twitch or point-and-click space game, and it is not
free-to-play. The engine is proprietary; the client is open for forking.
